assign.now: built — Socket.js reports state at reply time, MCP.js renders it and owns claim/release; docs repointed. Needs a dev-server restart + tab reload to verify.

log.msg: Tab.js needed NO change — settle() already passes the whole result object through, so the new visibility/focused/size fields reach MCP.js untouched. The wire was transparent; only the two ends needed editing.

assign.outcome: **The MCP layer now reports the tab state it answered in, and owns the claim verb.** A hidden tab does NOT sleep — it evaluates fine and stops *rendering*, so no rAF and no ResizeObserver; a geometry read still forces a reflow, which means CSS-driven layout measures true and only what the page sizes in a frame callback is frozen. That is a narrower and quieter trap than the one written down after `styles/layouts/space/`, where five screens all read 4184px because the generator resize never ran. Because visibility is TIME-VARYING — foreground when you spawn and claim a tab, hidden the moment the owner clicks away — a doc warning is a guess and a per-call report is a measurement: `Socket.js` now attaches `visibility`/`focused`/`size` inside `reply`, at answer time, and every `eval` answer ends with that state (loud when hidden, pointing at `shot`). `Tab.js` needed no change; `settle()` already passed the whole object through. `claim`/`release` are first-class MCP tools wrapping `dev/Claim`, replacing the `claim-tab` skill deleted in e92692c — the MCP `instructions` reach every session that HAS the tools, which is exactly the set that can claim anything, where a skill file must be found first. Five dead skill references cleared; `Claim/readme.md`, `Claim/page.js` and `Server/README.md` repointed. Playwright/CDP compared and declined for now: `site` owns the live tab, which no launcher-based tool can reach. NOT YET VERIFIED — the dev server is still the 1:07 PM process; restart it and reload a tab, then eval once in front and once clicked-away and watch `visibility` flip.
